purpose: Source-supported uncertainty ranges for per-serving nutrient inputs to FridgeLuck health scoring. These ranges drive the perturbation bounds in perturbation_bounds.json.
retrieval_note: Figures below were retrieved on 2026-10-10 via web research (Perplexity Sonar) during the session that authored this study. Each sourced figure names its citation. Entries marked judgment_call are explicitly labeled assumptions and are NOT attributed to any external source.

repo_internal_evidence.portion_benchmark_docs: planning/stage_4-gemini_live/confidence-engine-spec.md (line ~210) defines 'Portion MAE and macro MAE against corrected/ground-truth entries' as planned evaluation metrics but records NO measured figures at base commit 8c9c88f. The in-repo Nutrition5k benchmark (PR #41, RGB / RGB+D / foodlist arms) had 11 tests passing with evaluation pending at the time of writing, so no measured in-repo MAE figure exists to cite yet.
repo_internal_evidence.adopted_posture: The project's Nutrition5k portion-experiment protocol requires reporting mass and energy separately with MAE, forbids presenting mean error as an individual guarantee, and forbids generalizing controlled cafeteria/depth results to marker-free phone photos. This study adopts the same posture: the ranges below are population-level error envelopes used to stress a ranking function, not guarantees about any single meal, and clinical interpretation is out of scope (see report scope fences).

modeling_choice.form: multiplicative symmetric: each nutrient x is perturbed to x * (1 + u), u ~ Uniform(-b, +b) with b the bound in percent; exact zeros stay zero
modeling_choice.justification: Uniform draws give honest finite intervals for overlap analysis; a symmetric envelope is a deliberately simple, transparent choice.
modeling_choice.caveat: The sourced figures are MEAN ABSOLUTE errors (MAE / PMAE), not symmetric bounds. Using a MAE figure as a symmetric bound treats 'typical' error as the envelope and understates the tails; the separately labeled stress/adversarial arms exist to probe the tails. This mismatch is stated, not hidden.

calories.plausible_citation: Thames et al., 'Nutrition5k: Towards Automatic Nutritional Understanding of Generic Food', CVPR 2021 (arXiv:2103.03375): calorie prediction PMAE 16.5% (~67.4 kcal MAE) for the best RGB-D mass-estimation model. Corroborating figure: DPF-Nutrition (arXiv:2310.11702) reports calorie PMAE 14.7% on Nutrition5k.
calories.stress_basis: Judgment call: roughly 2x the plausible bound; above the 18% mean overage of measured vs stated calories in Urban et al. 2010 (PubMed 20102837) and below the 48% side-order overage in Urban et al. 2011 (JAMA 296(2)).

protein.plausible_citation: DPF-Nutrition (arXiv:2310.11702), per-nutrient PMAE on Nutrition5k: protein 20.2%. Corroborating figure: Thames et al. CVPR 2021 reports 26.2% aggregate MAE across fat, carbohydrate, and protein.
protein.stress_basis: Judgment call: ~2x the plausible bound, above the 26.2% aggregate macro MAE reported by Thames et al. CVPR 2021.

carbs.plausible_citation: DPF-Nutrition (arXiv:2310.11702), per-nutrient PMAE on Nutrition5k: carbohydrate 20.7%.
carbs.stress_basis: Judgment call: ~2x the plausible bound, above the 26.2% aggregate macro MAE (Thames et al. CVPR 2021).

fat.plausible_citation: DPF-Nutrition (arXiv:2310.11702), per-nutrient PMAE on Nutrition5k: fat 22.6%.
fat.stress_basis: Judgment call: ~1.8x the plausible bound, above the 26.2% aggregate macro MAE (Thames et al. CVPR 2021).

fiber.plausible_basis: Judgment call: no image-based fiber MAE figure was found in the sources retrieved for this study. Anchored to (a) the FDA nutrition-label tolerance that naturally occurring nutrients be at or above 80% of declared value (retrieved secondary source describing FDA compliance classes), and (b) an interlaboratory USDA study reporting more than 20% unacceptable Z'-scores for dietary fiber analyses (Anal Bioanal Chem 389:219-229, via ars.usda.gov) - an analytical-agreement statistic, not a food-variability figure.

sugar.plausible_basis: Judgment call: no image-based sugar MAE figure was found in the sources retrieved. Anchored to the FDA nutrition-label tolerance that calories, sugars, and total fat must not exceed 120% of declared values (retrieved secondary source describing FDA compliance classes).

sodium.plausible_basis: Judgment call: no image-based sodium MAE figure was found in the sources retrieved. Anchored to the FDA 120%-of-declared label tolerance and to the interlaboratory USDA study reporting more than 20% unacceptable Z'-scores for sodium analyses, disproportionately in low-sodium matrices (Anal Bioanal Chem 389:219-229, via ars.usda.gov).

portion_scale.unit: multiplicative scale on all per-serving values
portion_scale.plausible_citation: Thames et al., CVPR 2021 (arXiv:2103.03375): mass estimation MAE 10.6% (~22.3 g) for the best RGB-D model.
portion_scale.bridging_judgment: Bridging judgment (flagged): Nutrition5k mass error is plate-level; we use it as a proxy for per-serving scaling error. The protocol caveat about generalizing controlled cafeteria results applies.
portion_scale.stress_basis: Urban et al. 2011 (JAMA 296(2)) found side orders measured 48% above stated calories on average; that one-sided restaurant finding is used here, symmetrically, as the stress tail. Flagged judgment: the source figure is one-sided and about restaurant side orders, not home portions.

usda_note: No universal USDA FoodData Central coefficient of variation for protein/fiber/sodium could be cited: the research retrieval for this study found that USDA-wide percent-variability figures are not defensible without naming food, data type, and comparison method; FDC Foundation Foods documentation instead exposes per-sample variability. Per-nutrient judgment calls above are the consequence, stated openly.

never_perturbed.what: Ranking weights and constants (72.0, 2.5, 6.5, 8.0, +6/+3 time, +5/-3/+3 goal, +4 high-protein, 24.0 missing penalty, +10 bonuses, 20-point rating divisor), user profile values (dailyCalories, macro percentages, goal), match inputs (matched/total/optional/missing counts), timeMinutes, tags, and personalScore.
never_perturbed.why: The study asks how ranking responds to NUTRIENT/PORTION uncertainty. Perturbing model constants or user-stated profile values would answer a different question.
